title: America mein qibla north-east kyun? (talking head)

lines.line: America mein Muslim namaz *north-east* ki taraf muh karke padhte hain.

options.visual: 0.0: real photo of worshippers in the Islamic Center of Washington's prayer hall (USIA, public domain), darkened, pushing in; a huge compass ring over it, needle already swinging. 1.2 ("north-east"): needle locks on NE, turns orange, NORTH-EAST slams up. 1.9: hard cut to the mosque's minaret against blue sky (colour), an orange arrow drawn up-right.
options.sound: impact on frame 0, tick on the lock, whoosh on the cut
options.why: Frame 0 is a real mosque with a bold one-word question; the needle moves from frame 0; three beats before 2 s.

options.visual: 0.0: the globe fills the frame, spinning; 0.8: it brakes on North America, a pin drops on Washington; 1.2: an orange arrow leaves the pin up-right, NORTH-EAST.
options.sound: riser into a thud on the pin
options.why: Sets up the globe world early, but a spinning globe is a common opener and less specific than a real mosque.

options.visual: 0.0: the classroom map already zoomed on the North Atlantic, Washington pin, both arrows drawn: orange NE and white SE, with a ? between them. 1.2: the NE arrow pulses.
options.why: Shows the whole contradiction at once, but gives away line 2 before it is said and has no real image.

lines.line: Par map kholo, toh Makkah wahan se *south-east* mein dikhta hai.

options.visual: 2.73 (creator's cut): hard cut to the Mercator classroom map (built from NASA Blue Marble, public domain), framed on the North Atlantic; pins WASHINGTON and MAKKAH. 3.56 ("Makkah"): a straight white line draws from Washington to Makkah, down-right. 4.22 ("south-east"): SOUTH-EAST slams beside the line, and the orange NE arrow from the hook flashes back on the same pin: two directions, one city.
options.sound: whoosh on the cut, marker squeak on the line, hit on SOUTH-EAST
options.why: The contradiction is drawn on the map the viewer knows; muted, the first 6 s read: QIBLA NORTH-EAST / MAP SOUTH-EAST.

options.visual: The compass (top) and the map (bottom) side by side; the map's line draws on "Makkah".
options.why: Clear comparison, but a split this early shrinks both pictures below thumbnail strength.

options.visual: The creator appears; a small map card beside his head shows the SE line.
options.why: Puts the creator on screen at 2.8 s, earlier than the hook rule wants; the map is too small to read.

lines.line: 1953 mein Washington ki ek nayi masjid ke saath yahi hua.

options.visual: 5.27 (creator's cut): the speaker slides into the top window, first time on screen; below, the 1954 UPI photo of the mosque nearly finished (public domain, B&W) rises in, slow push. WASHINGTON DC · 1953 lands on "1953"; a small 'photo: 1954' under it.
options.why: The story starts on a real archival picture while the creator finally shows his face.

options.visual: The 1954 photo full frame with the date over it.
options.why: Stronger photo, but keeps the creator off screen until 8.3 s.

lines.line: Uska rukh north-east rakha gaya, aur dekhne wale ghabra gaye ki masjid galat taraf ban rahi hai.

options.layout: full-screen graphic, then speaker + chest card
options.visual: 8.33: hard cut to a big compass dial on chart paper; the mosque's outline turns from north to 56 degrees, the number rolls up to 56°33′ ("north-east"), source line The Washington Daily News, 15 April 1953. 9.97 (creator's cut): back to the speaker; on his chest a paper card with the passers-by's words from the same paper, "Take any map… the line would go slightly south." On "galat" (11.58) a WRONG WAY? stamp hits the card.
options.text: FACES 56°33′ EAST OF NORTH / "Take any map… the line would go slightly south."
options.why: Uses the real 1953 numbers and the real words people said, instead of an invented reaction.

options.visual: The map with a crowd of ? marks around Washington; speaker in the corner circle.
options.why: Simple, but the ? icons are decoration and lose the real quote.

lines.line: Masjid *galat* nahi thi. Gadbad us map mein thi, jo hum school se dekhte aa rahe hain.

options.layout: speaker full screen, then full-screen B-roll
options.visual: 12.63: speaker, punch-in on "galat". 15.10 (creator's cut, "jo hum school se"): a wall map, a hand moving across it (Pexels 8829564), tag THE MAP FROM SCHOOL.
options.why: The punch carries the reversal; the wall-map shot makes 'that map' concrete in 1.5 s.

options.visual: Punch-in on "galat", wider on "Gadbad".
options.why: Keeps the creator's authority on the reversal, but misses the chance to show the map.

lines.line: Map flat hai, aur zameen gol.

options.visual: 16.67: top half the flat map lands on "flat" (FLAT), bottom half the 3D globe turning lands on "gol" (ROUND).
options.why: The whole idea of the reel in two words and two pictures.

options.visual: Card FLAT MAP vs ROUND EARTH.
options.why: Lighter, but the idea is visual and deserves pictures.

lines.line: Ek santre ka chhilka utaro, aur use table par bilkul flat karke dikhao.

options.visual: 18.37: real close-up of hands peeling a large orange in one piece (Pexels 6535276, 4K) in the lower board, the speaker above. Label TRY THIS: LAY THE PEEL FLAT on "flat karke dikhao".
options.text: TRY THIS: LAY THE PEEL FLAT
options.sound: soft whoosh as the board rises
options.why: A real, tactile demo everyone has done; the creator stays on screen giving the challenge.

options.visual: The peel clip full frame.
options.why: Bigger fruit, but no face for 8 s with the next graphic.

lines.line: Nahi hoga. Kahin phatega, kahin *stretch* ho jaayega.

options.visual: 21.80: an orange skin splits into 8 petals that fall flat onto paper. 23.02 ("phatega"): the gaps between petals flash, TEARS. 23.82 ("stretch"): the petals stretch sideways until the gaps close into a rectangle, STRETCHES.
options.sound: tick on TEARS, whoosh on STRETCHES
options.why: Turns the spoken demo into an exact picture of what a map does.

options.visual: TEARS and STRETCHES as chips beside the face.
options.why: Cheap; the idea needs to be seen.

lines.line: Duniya ka map bhi aise hi khincha hua hai.

options.visual: 24.73: the same petals swap their orange skin for the Earth (NASA Blue Marble) and stretch into the world map; Greenland swells as the map stretches towards the poles. 26.18 ("khincha"): GREENLAND and AFRICA marked, chip AFRICA IS 14x BIGGER.
options.text: GREENLAND looks as big as AFRICA / AFRICA IS 14x BIGGER
options.why: Proves 'stretched' with the most famous example; the flat-earth viewers said the concept was unclear, this makes it unmissable.

options.visual: The finished map only, with STRETCHED stamped on it.
options.why: Says it without showing how.

lines.line: Isliye map par jo line seedhi dikhti hai, wo zameen par sabse chhota raasta nahi hoti.

options.visual: 26.80 (creator's cut): the classroom map again with the hook's straight white line, label STRAIGHT ON THE MAP; the speaker in the corner circle. 29.42 ("sabse chhota"): NOT THE SHORTEST stamps on the white line.
options.text: STRAIGHT ON THE MAP / NOT THE SHORTEST
options.why: Calls back the hook's line and states the rule while the creator stays visible.

options.visual: Same without the circle.
options.why: Cleaner, but a long stretch without the face.

lines.line: Ab ek globe par Washington se Makkah tak ek dhaaga *tight* karke lagao.

options.visual: 30.60: the 3D globe (NASA texture) turns to the Atlantic; pins land on WASHINGTON (31.40) and MAKKAH (31.94); 33.08 ("tight"): an orange string snaps tight between them along the great circle.
options.why: The globe is the answer; the string is a physical, testable demo.

options.visual: Same, no circle.
options.why: More globe, less creator.

lines.line: Dhaaga pehle upar ki taraf jaata hai, north-east.

options.visual: 34.23: camera close on Washington; the string leaves up and to the right; a compass badge on the pin points along it: STARTS NORTH-EAST (36.12).
options.why: The single fact the whole reel turns on, shown at the pin.

options.visual: The great circle drawn on the flat map as a curve.
options.why: Less physical than the globe.

lines.line: Phir Atlantic aur Europe ke upar se mudta hai, aur Makkah par utarta hai.

options.visual: 36.77: the camera rides along the string over the ocean: ATLANTIC (37.02), EUROPE (37.62), bends down and lands on MAKKAH (39.10).
options.why: The surprising route (over Europe) is the 'wow' viewers share.

options.visual: Same route on the flat map.
options.why: Weaker.

lines.line: Wo pehli direction hi Washington ka pehla qibla hai.

options.visual: 40.10 (creator's cut): back to the compass dial from line 4; the string's first direction drops into it and matches the mosque's 56 degrees: QIBLA = FIRST DIRECTION · 56° NE.
options.why: Closes the loop with the 1953 number.

options.visual: Card QIBLA = 56° NE.
options.why: Lighter.

lines.line: Toh masjid bilkul *sahi* bani thi.

options.visual: 42.60 (creator's cut): speaker, punch-in on "sahi"; an orange tick chip RIGHT ALL ALONG on the chest.
options.why: The verdict belongs to the creator's face.

options.visual: The minaret photo with a tick.
options.why: Loses the face at the verdict.

lines.line: Alaska mein toh qibla seedha, lagbhag *north* ki taraf hai, pole ke upar se.

options.visual: 44.07: the globe swings so the North Pole faces the camera; pin on ALASKA; the orange string goes up over the pole and down to Makkah. 46.16 ("north"): ALMOST DUE NORTH · 351°.
options.why: The most surprising case, and only a globe can show it.

options.visual: Alaska's line drawn on the flat map.
options.why: On a flat map it looks absurd, which is the point, but harder to read.

lines.line: Muslim astronomers ye hisaab hazaar saal pehle hi spherical trigonometry se laga rahe the.

options.visual: 47.83 (creator's cut): al-Biruni's astronomy diagram from Kitab al-Tafhim (public domain, c. 1029 CE) on the board, slow push; label 1,000 YEARS AGO; 50.26 ("spherical trigonometry"): a spherical triangle draws over a small globe beside it.
options.why: A real manuscript of a Muslim astronomer; no portraits.

options.visual: Indo-Persian astrolabe, 1601 (Art Institute of Chicago, CC0).
options.why: Beautiful, but 1601 is not 1,000 years ago.

lines.line: Waise America ki kuch masjidein aaj bhi south-east ki taraf hain.

options.layout: speaker full screen + mid-video follow card
options.visual: 51.87 (creator's cut): the honest beat to camera, no graphic; the Follow card sits on the chest for 2.5 s, clear of the face and the right rail.
options.why: Honesty lands best from the face; the one speaker stretch long enough for the mid-video CTA.

options.visual: North America with a few SE arrows among many NE.
options.why: Would need a survey we don't have.

lines.line: Aur itni door se Kaaba ki direction ki taraf muh karna hi kaafi hai, ye bahut se scholars ki raay hai.

options.visual: 55.23 (creator's cut): torn-paper card, 2:144 from src/data/quran/2-144.json, the part from "fa walli wajhaka shatra" (cut by code), Sahih International below; 58.24 ("scholars"): a note slides up: Many scholars: from far away, facing the direction is enough. For your own case, ask a scholar.
options.text: 2:144 · Turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram / SCHOLARLY VIEW
options.why: Shows where 'direction' comes from without issuing a ruling. Needs the creator's OK because the Ayah is not spoken.

options.visual: The scholarly note only.
options.why: Safer, plainer.

lines.line: Map *jhooth* nahi bolta. Bas gol duniya ko flat dikhane mein thoda *khinch* jaata hai.

options.visual: 59.63: speaker, punch on "jhooth". 61.00 (creator's cut): the flat map wraps itself back round the globe; the orange string is on both. THE MAP ISN'T LYING. IT'S STRETCHED. lands and holds still to the end of the line.
options.text: THE MAP ISN'T LYING. / IT'S STRETCHED.
options.sound: soft whoosh, hit on the line
options.why: Ends on the reel's one idea as a picture: flat and round.
Misses the visual payoff.

lines.line: Follow kar lo, aise hi fascinating videos ke liye.

options.visual: 63.73 (creator's cut): Follow card in the caption band (Instagram + Facebook icons, unaltered) and the comment card in the headroom: "What's the qibla direction from your city?"
options.text: Follow / What's the qibla direction from your city?
options.why: The comment question invites every viewer to work out their own city.
No comment prompt.
